thread:
elena: Heads-up — Prospecta (sales) sent a draft: they want reserved capacity + a sizable burst pool. Asking for 250 GPU-equivalents reserved in us-west and a 30% cross-region burst credit for Q1. Can infra sanity-check cost and feasibility? :eyes:
matt: Quick sanity check: 250 GPUs baseline -> `250 * 24 * 30 = 180000 GPU-hours/mo`. With 30% burst credit that's another `54k` GPU-hours available for spikes, so planning capacity footprint ~234k GPU-hours. Are we treating burst as additive capacity or pre-funded credit?
kai: We usually model burst as pre-funded credits that map to transient instances rather than permanently reserved nodes. Pros: cheaper overall. Con: scheduling complexity + warm pool hit if burst used frequently. Region note: us-west primary, but they want to spill to us-east and eu-west if us-west saturated. Network egress + cross-region provisioning ops need to be clarified.
elena: Sales says they expect most traffic in us-west but will failover to eu-west for DR. They explicitly want predictable latency <= 150ms p95 for generation.
matt: p95 150ms with A100s is doable for our mid-sized models with right batching. If they want H100 performance equivalent, we'd shrink GPU count but costs change. Do we have a quick cost delta mapping?
mohit: From finance: ballpark reserved price we offered before was $X/hour for A100-equivalent reserved. If they convert to H100-equivalent, multiply by ~1.8 on price but reduce GPU count roughly same factor. I'll run numbers but need the GPU-hour breakdown by instance type.
kai: For modelling, two quick scenarios:
- A100 baseline: 250 reserved, 30% burst -> spare transient capacity, warm pool of ~10% to reduce cold-start latency.
- H100 baseline: ~140 reserved (perf parity), 30% burst -> still need warm pool, but density changes rack/network load.

We should also account for KV cache RAM and networking. Cross-region burst will increase egress and model-sync traffic.
matt: Ops questions: how often do we expect bursts? If bursts < 5% of minutes, credits approach works. If bursts are sustained (e.g., daily peak windows), we need permanent headroom or staged autoscale. Can we ask sales for hourly profile?
elena: I'll request an hourly 7-day sample from the prospect. They only gave monthly QPS estimates right now.
mohit: Also need commitment term — 12mo vs 36mo changes effective price and whether we recommend reserved + credits or reserved + guaranteed burst pool (dedicated burst servers). Finance prefers reserved + credits for smaller terms.
kai: Technical constraint: our scheduler cannot instantly spin H100s in eu-west because we have limited H100 inventory there. If their spillover target is eu-west, burst credit must map to A100 transient instances which might not meet latency for heavy models. So routing policy needs to be region-aware and model-aware.
matt: Suggest we propose two options in the deal:
1) Conservative: 250 A100-reserved in us-west, 30% burst credits usable in us-west only. Includes 10% warm pool. (Lower operational risk).
2) Flexible: 170 H100-equivalent reserved in us-west, 30% burst credits cross-region allowed but only for best-effort workloads; DR traffic routed to eu-west with relaxed p95 target.

Callouts: include a clause for 'spike abuse' — if burst utilization > 35% sustained for >72h, auto-convert some credits into short-term reserved billing or throttle.
elena: Sales wants a single proposal doc. Can infra produce the two option numbers (GPU-hours, estimated monthly cost, expected p95) by EOD tomorrow?
matt: I can draft the A100 numbers and the warm-pool sizing. Will need support from mohit for $ numbers and from kai for region feasibility.
kai: I'll check inventory (H100 vs A100) in us-west/us-east/eu-west and run a quick simulation for spilling patterns. ETA: 12h.
mohit: I'll model pricing for 12mo and 36mo, include expected effective hourly rate and projected overage cost for burst-to-transient mapping.
elena: Great. Also add a one-sentence operational playbook for on-call: who to page if burst causes cross-region autoscale? Prefer ops-runbook link.
matt: Add `#oncall` as contact. Ops playbook lines I suggest: 1) if cross-region cold starts >3 per hour, page infra oncall; 2) enable temporary throttles; 3) enable queued fallback model (smaller model) to preserve latency.
ops-bot: Reminder: runbook template updated: https://intra.redwood/runbooks/prospecta-capacity-template (automated) :white_check_mark:
elena: Perfect. I'll consolidate responses and push to sales. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
matt: One more thought — include explicit quant: "burst credits are non-guaranteed, can be reclaimed with 24h notice" in contract. Reduces risk.
kai: Agree. Also flag that cross-region burst implies additional costs for model replication; add a one-time sync fee if they want multi-region full model copies.
mohit: Noted. I'll add a line for expected one-time sync cost and a per-GPU-hour overage rate.
elena: OK closing thread — will post the prospect's hourly profile when I get it.
